title: Short: "The Earth turns while you fall"

lines.text: Lower a probe into a tunnel dug right on the equator.
The Earth turns once every twenty-three point nine hours.
That carries the equator east at about sixteen hundred and seventy kilometres an hour.
That's the speed of the ground itself, right where the tunnel starts.
The probe is carried along with it, sideways.
It keeps that sideways speed as it falls.
But the rock deeper down is closer to the axis, so it's moving slower.
So the probe drifts sideways, faster than the wall beside it, and the gap keeps growing as it sinks.
lines.cue: caption: IT DRIFTS FASTER THAN THE WALL

lines.text: So where would you dig the tunnel, so the probe falls straight? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
